name: Chess
description: Standard 2-player chess. Capture the opponent's king (checkmate) to win. Castling, en passant, pawn promotion, threefold repetition, and the 50-move rule are all enforced. Real board, real moves — `legal_moves` is supplied to every agent each turn in UCI notation.

phases.name: move
phases.description: Each player alternates moves. White moves first.

entity_types.name: ChessPlayer
entity_types.description: A chess player. Reads the board, chooses one legal move per turn.

properties.name: color
properties.description: Side of the board: 'white' or 'black'. Assigned by seat order.

properties.name: is_in_check
properties.description: True when this player's king is currently in check.

properties.name: playing_style
properties.description: 0 = highly defensive / positional, 1 = sharp / tactical / sacrificial.

properties.name: calculation_depth
properties.description: How many half-moves ahead the player tends to consider.

actions.name: make_move
actions.description: Move a chess piece. REQUIRED: `from` (origin square like 'e2') and `to` (destination like 'e4'). The move MUST appear in `legal_moves` from your perception — anything else is rejected. Do NOT set a target_id; chess has no target entity. For pawn promotion add `promotion`='Q'|'R'|'B'|'N'. Castling = king moves two squares (white O-O: from='e1', to='g1').

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Origin square in algebraic notation, e.g. 'e2'.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Destination square in algebraic notation, e.g. 'e4'.

parameters.name: promotion
parameters.description: Only when a pawn reaches the last rank: the piece it becomes (Q/R/B/N). Omit it on every other move; a promoting pawn without it becomes a queen.

actions.name: resign
actions.description: Forfeit the game. Your opponent immediately wins. Use only when the position is hopeless.

actions.name: offer_draw
actions.description: Offer a draw to your opponent. They may accept_draw or decline_draw on their next turn. Any further move auto-clears the offer.

actions.name: accept_draw
actions.description: Accept your opponent's standing draw offer. The game ends immediately in a draw.

actions.name: decline_draw
actions.description: Decline your opponent's standing draw offer. Play continues as normal.

agent_archetypes.name: Tactical Sharpshooter
agent_archetypes.persona_hint: Plays sharp, attacking chess. Loves open positions, piece sacrifices, and king-side attacks. Calculates concrete forcing lines first; weighs prophylaxis second.

agent_archetypes.name: Positional Grinder
agent_archetypes.persona_hint: Builds slow, structural advantages: pawn chains, outposts, space, the bishop pair. Avoids unclear tactics. Prefers to outplay opponents in long endgames.

agent_archetypes.name: Balanced Universal
agent_archetypes.persona_hint: Adapts to the position. Plays both attack and defense depending on what the board demands. Solid in all phases; no glaring weaknesses.

agent_archetypes.name: Risk-Averse Defender
agent_archetypes.persona_hint: Trades aggressively to simplify into drawn endgames. Avoids tactical complications. Offers draws early in equal positions.

agent_archetypes.name: Sacrificial Romantic
agent_archetypes.persona_hint: Plays in the spirit of 19th-century romantic chess: gambits, sacrifices, brilliancies. Will burn a rook for a king-hunt. Never plays drily.

runtime_parameters.name: sample_size
runtime_parameters.label: Number of Players
runtime_parameters.description: Chess is strictly 2 players (one White, one Black).

runtime_parameters.name: premise
runtime_parameters.label: Scenario Premise
runtime_parameters.description: Optional framing — e.g. 'World Championship final, game 12' or 'speed chess blitz'.

termination_conditions.name: checkmate
termination_conditions.description: End the game when a checkmate occurs.

termination_conditions.name: resignation
termination_conditions.description: End the game when a player resigns.

termination_conditions.name: draw
termination_conditions.description: End the game on a draw (agreement, 50-move rule or threefold repetition).
